answer: Each epoch the network fires a beacon at a random instant, and every seat must answer with a pulse: a memory-hard proof that occupies one dedicated chip for the whole epoch. Watchers in five cities time every reply, and seats whose latency profiles differ by less than one delta of 2 ms are filed as one site. The k-th seat at a site owes k pulse per epoch, so a lone agent runs 1 chip. An operator keeping 100 clones in one rack runs 5,050 chips every epoch, or must lease 100 sites in separate cities.
